<Route path="/ade/dashboard/catalog/[id]?tab=workflows" />

An [Arazzo](https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/latest.html) document describes **workflows**:
ordered steps, each calling an operation of an API (or another workflow), with the inputs the
workflow takes, the outputs it returns, and what happens when a step succeeds or fails. The
**Workflows** tab shows each workflow as that flow — a list of steps, a step graph, and the
operation each step calls — instead of as a file.

## Where the tab appears

- **A catalog item imported from an Arazzo document.** **Open the item** from **Catalog** and
  **select the “Workflows” tab**, the last tab on the item's page. Its count is the number of
  workflows in the item's latest revision. The address is `?tab=workflows`, so you can send it to a
  teammate.
- **A project whose HEAD revision holds workflows.** **Open the project** on **Versions** and
  **select the “Workflows” tab** beside **Dependencies**. The tab reads the HEAD revision, and a
  project with no workflows has no tab. `?tab=workflows` opens it directly.

The tab reads nothing until you select it.

<Screenshot id="arazzo-workflows" alt="The Workflows tab: the checkout and send-receipt workflows on the left; on the right the checkout workflow's source descriptions (shop resolved, payments missing), its inputs and outputs, its three steps, and the step graph" />

## Read a workflow

1. **Pick a workflow** in the **Workflows** list on the left. Each entry shows its `workflowId`,
   its summary, how many steps it has and, in red, how many of its sources are missing. The first
   workflow is open when the tab loads.
2. Read **Source descriptions**: every API description the workflow's steps call, with its
   status.

   | Status | Meaning |
   | --- | --- |
   | **Resolved** | The import found the description — **from fileset** (in the same upload, archive or repository selection), **from catalog** (a spec you had already imported) or **from remote** (fetched from its URL) |
   | **Missing** | No source was found. The reason code beside it — such as `not-in-fileset` or `resolution-disabled` — says why; hover it for the detail. See [Import an Arazzo workflow with its API files](../bring-in/import-a-spec.md#import-an-arazzo-workflow-with-its-api-files) |
   | **Not recorded** | The revision was imported before Apiome recorded where sources came from. Re-import it to find out |

3. Read **Inputs** — each top-level property of the workflow's `inputs` schema, its type and
   whether it is required (or the `$ref` the schema points at) — and **Outputs**, each name with
   the runtime expression that produces it, such as `$steps.pay.outputs.receipt`.
4. Read **Steps**, in the order the document declares them. Each row shows the `stepId` and what
   it calls: the method and route of the operation (`GET /carts/{cartId}`), the raw `operationId`
   or `operationRef` when it was not resolved (marked **Not resolved**), or **Calls workflow** for a
   step that runs another workflow.

## The step graph

Under the steps, **Step graph** draws the workflow's routing from **Start** to **End**:

| Edge | Drawn when |
| --- | --- |
| **Next step** (grey) | A step has no `onSuccess` actions, so it continues to the next step — or, as the last step, to **End** |
| **On success** (green) | An `onSuccess` action: `goto` a step or workflow, or `end` |
| **On failure** (red, dashed) | An `onFailure` action, or — when a step has none — the step failing the workflow, drawn to **Failed** |
| **Retry** (amber, dotted) | A `retry` action that names another step or workflow |

Each edge is labelled with its action's `name`. A step that retries *itself* carries a
**retry ×3** badge instead of a loop. When every action of a step is conditional (has `criteria`),
the default path is drawn as well, since the step falls through when no criteria match. A called
workflow sits above the row — **select it** to show that workflow — and so does a reusable
`$components` action, which the graph labels but does not follow.

<Screenshot id="arazzo-workflow-graph" alt="The step graph of the checkout workflow: Start, load-cart, pay with a retry ×3 badge, notify and End along one row, a green to-pay edge from load-cart to pay, and red dashed edges down to Failed" />

## Open a step and its operation

**Click a step** in **Steps** or in the graph (or **Tab** to it and press <Kbd keys="Enter"/>) to
open its drawer:

- **Operation** — for a resolved step, the operation it calls: method and route, summary,
  description, `operationId`, the project or catalog item that holds it, its **Parameters** and its
  **Responses**. **“Open project”** (or **“Open catalog item”**) at the bottom goes there. A step
  whose reference was not resolved says why instead, and shows the reference as written; a step
  that calls a workflow offers **“Show workflow”**.
- **Step parameters**, **Request body**, **Success criteria**, **On success**, **On failure** and
  **Outputs** — the step as the document wrote it, with each action spelled out, such as
  *Go to step pay* or *Retry up to 3 times, 1 s apart*.

<Screenshot id="arazzo-workflow-step" alt="The step drawer for load-cart open over the Workflows tab: GET /carts/{cartId}, its parameters and responses, the step's success criteria and its on-success and on-failure actions" />

Press <Kbd keys="Esc"/> or **“Close”** to return to the tab.

A step resolves when the operation it names was imported in the same scan — for example, the
OpenAPI file in the same archive or repository selection. The link is kept by id, so deleting that
operation later turns the step back into an unresolved one.

## Empty and error states

- **No workflows** — the revision holds no Arazzo workflows (for example, the document declares
  none).
- **Couldn't load the workflows** — the read failed; the message says why, and **“Try again”**
  retries it.
- In the drawer, **Couldn't load the operation** — the operation could not be read; **“Try again”**
  retries it.

## With the API

- `GET /v1/workflows/{tenant_slug}/catalog/{item_id}` — the workflows of a catalog item's latest
  revision.
- `GET /v1/workflows/{tenant_slug}/versions/{version_id}` — the workflows of any revision.
- `GET /v1/workflows/{tenant_slug}/operations/{path_operation_id}` — one operation a step calls,
  with its parameters and responses.

See [Arazzo workflows](../reference/rest/arazzo-workflows.md) in the REST reference.
